subject: Introduction to Mechanical Engineering
sourceBasis: ACADRIX R-2025 Unit I scope: history and evolution of Mechanical Engineering; force, motion, energy, work and power; units and dimensions; SI system; ethics and professionalism. Prescribed-book themes: Wickert & Lewis and R. K. Rajput.
note: Original ACADRIX exam-practice questions; not claimed official university questions or verified PYQs.

questions.question: Explain the major stages in the history and evolution of Mechanical Engineering, relating developments in machines, power and manufacturing to the growth of the profession.
solutionPlan: Introduce the early use of simple machines.
Discuss development of mechanisms, machine tools and power systems.
Explain the impact of steam power and mechanised production.
Connect industrial development to the modern Mechanical Engineering profession.
Conclude with modern interdisciplinary practice.

questions.question: Explain the role, scope and major responsibilities of a Mechanical Engineer in modern engineering practice.
solutionPlan: Define Mechanical Engineering.
Discuss design, analysis, manufacturing, operation and maintenance roles.
Relate mechanics, materials, thermal and manufacturing knowledge.
Include safety, sustainability and professional responsibility.
Give representative industry applications.

questions.question: Explain force as a vector quantity and demonstrate the resolution and combination of forces for a basic mechanical engineering problem.
solutionPlan: Define force and identify its magnitude, direction and line of action.
Resolve the force into suitable components.
Sum components to obtain the resultant.
Determine resultant magnitude and direction.
Interpret the result for the mechanical system.

questions.question: State and explain Newton's three laws of motion and illustrate their significance with Mechanical Engineering examples.
solutionPlan: State the first law and inertia.
State the second law and ΣF=ma.
State the third law and action-reaction pairs.
Give appropriate machine/vehicle/structure examples.
Distinguish the role of each law in analysis.

questions.question: Explain displacement, velocity and acceleration and derive the basic relationships among them for one-dimensional motion.
solutionPlan: Define displacement, velocity and acceleration.
Write v=ds/dt and a=dv/dt.
For constant acceleration, state the standard kinematic relations.
Explain the physical meaning of signs and units.
Relate the quantities to a mechanical motion example.

questions.question: Explain the concepts of work and mechanical energy and use the work-energy principle for a simple mechanical system.
solutionPlan: Define work and write W=Fs cosθ for constant force.
Define kinetic and potential energy.
State the work-energy principle.
Set up the energy balance for the system.
Interpret the final result with units.

questions.question: Explain power as a rate of energy transfer and solve a representative mechanical power problem.
solutionPlan: Define power as dW/dt.
Distinguish average and instantaneous power.
Use P=W/t or the appropriate mechanical relation.
Maintain consistent SI units.
Interpret the power requirement or output.

questions.question: Explain the SI system, fundamental and derived units, and dimensional representation of important mechanical quantities.
solutionPlan: Introduce the SI system and base quantities.
Identify relevant base units.
Derive units of force, work, energy, power and pressure.
Write their dimensions.
Explain why consistent units are essential in engineering calculations.

questions.question: Use dimensional analysis to check the dimensional homogeneity of a mechanical engineering equation and identify an inconsistent expression if present.
solutionPlan: Write dimensions of every physical quantity.
Substitute dimensions into each term.
Compare dimensions term by term.
Identify whether the equation is homogeneous.
Explain any required correction without changing unsupported quantities.

questions.question: Perform a systematic conversion of a mechanical quantity between SI and another unit system while preserving dimensional consistency.
solutionPlan: Write the given quantity with units.
Use appropriate conversion factors.
Cancel units step by step.
Check the final dimensions and magnitude.
Report the converted value clearly.

questions.question: Explain conservation of energy and apply an energy balance to a simple ideal mechanical system involving kinetic, potential and work interactions.
solutionPlan: State the conservation principle.
Identify initial and final energy forms.
Account for work interaction where applicable.
Form the energy balance.
Solve and interpret the result.

questions.question: Discuss the ethical responsibilities of a Mechanical Engineer with emphasis on public safety, competence, honesty, conflicts of interest and environmental responsibility.
solutionPlan: Explain engineering ethics and professional responsibility.
Discuss protection of public safety and welfare.
Explain competence and responsible technical judgement.
Discuss honesty and conflicts of interest.
Include environmental and sustainability considerations.

questions.question: Analyse a hypothetical engineering decision in which safety, cost, technical competence and environmental impact conflict, and explain how a responsible Mechanical Engineer should approach the decision.
solutionPlan: Identify stakeholders and technical constraints.
Prioritise safety and applicable requirements.
Separate facts from assumptions.
Seek competent review where expertise is insufficient.
Compare alternatives and document the responsible decision.

questions.question: Solve an integrated introductory mechanics problem requiring force, motion, work-energy and power concepts, and present the solution using consistent SI units.
solutionPlan: Draw or describe the mechanical situation.
Identify forces and motion variables.
Select Newtonian or energy methods as appropriate.
Calculate work/energy and required power where applicable.
Check dimensions, signs and units.

questions.question: Explain how force, motion, energy, work, power, units and dimensions form the fundamental analytical language used by Mechanical Engineers.
solutionPlan: Define each foundational concept.
Show the mathematical relationships among them.
Connect dimensions and SI units to the relationships.
Use a simple machine or engineering system as an example.
Conclude with the importance of these foundations for later Mechanical Engineering subjects.

examChecklist: Define vector quantities clearly and preserve direction/sign conventions.
Use SI units consistently before numerical substitution.
Check dimensional homogeneity for derived equations.
Distinguish work, energy and power rather than treating them as interchangeable.
For motion problems, state the known quantities and assumptions.
For energy methods, identify every relevant energy/work term.
For ethics questions, explicitly address safety, competence, integrity, conflicts of interest and environmental responsibility.
